exams.title: Anatomy Comprehensive Practical Exam
exams.titleArabic: الامتحان العملي الشامل للتشريح (Anatomy Comprehensive Exam)
exams.description: Comprehensive timed medical OSPE practical exam covering major osteology bones (Femur, Tibia, Humerus, Scapula), muscle dissections, and joint kinesiology.

exams.title: Bones Practical Exam
exams.description: Focused OSPE station exam on identification of dry bones, bony landmarks, axes, and osteological features (Femur, Tibia, Humerus, Scapula, Mandible, Axial skeleton).

exams.title: Muscles Practical Exam
exams.description: Practical station exam on gross muscle dissections, origin/insertion landmarks, actions, and motor nerve supply (Biceps, Triceps, Deltoid, Pectoralis Major, Gastrocnemius).

exams.title: Movements & Joints Exam
exams.description: Practical kinesiology and arthrology exam evaluating anatomical plane movements (Flexion, Extension, Abduction) and knee joint stabilizing ligaments.

exams.title: Histology Microscopic Slide Identification Exam
exams.titleArabic: اختبار الشرائح المجهرية — معمل الأنسجة (Histology Lab)
exams.description: High-power photomicrograph identification of basic epithelia, cartilage, compact bone, muscle types, and blood cytology.

exams.title: Biochemistry Practical Laboratory Tests & Interpretation
exams.titleArabic: اختبار التفاعلات والتفسير البيوكيميائي — معمل الكيمياء الحيوية
exams.description: Identification of biochemical test tubes, reaction mechanisms (Benedict, Iodine, Biuret, Ninhydrin, Molisch, Barfoed, Seliwanoff, Sudan), and clinical interpretations.

exams.title: University Integrated Medical OSPE — Practical Examination
exams.description: Comprehensive timed medical OSCE/OSPE practical examination covering Anatomy osteology & myology, Histology epithelia & tissues, and Biochemistry diagnostic laboratory tests.

questions.questionText: Identify the bone shown in the anatomical specimen.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على العظمة الموضحة في الصورة التشريحية.
questions.explanation: The Femur (thigh bone) is the longest, heaviest, and strongest bone in the human body. Characterized by a spherical head, anatomical neck, greater and lesser trochanters, and distal condyles.
questions.clinicalNote: Femoral neck fractures are common in elderly osteoporotic patients and carry a high risk of avascular necrosis of the femoral head due to disruption of retinacular vessels.

questions.questionText: Identify the bone shown in the image.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على العظمة الموضحة في الصورة.
questions.explanation: The Tibia (shin bone) is the large, weight-bearing medial bone of the leg. Key features include the tibial tuberosity, anterior border (shin), and medial malleolus.
questions.clinicalNote: The subcutaneous anteromedial surface of the tibia is vulnerable to direct trauma and open (compound) fractures.

questions.questionText: Identify the upper limb bone shown in the osteology specimen.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على عظمة الطرف العلوي الموضحة في العينة العظمية.
questions.explanation: The Humerus is the single bone of the arm (brachium). Features include head, anatomical neck, surgical neck, greater & lesser tubercles, intertubercular sulcus, and distal capitulum & trochlea.
questions.clinicalNote: Fracture of the surgical neck can injure the axillary nerve; mid-shaft fractures risk injuring the radial nerve in the spiral groove.

questions.questionText: Identify the triangular flat bone of the shoulder girdle shown.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على العظمة المسطحة الموضحة في حزام الكتف.
questions.explanation: The Scapula (shoulder blade) is a triangular flat bone located posterolaterally on the thoracic cage over ribs 2 to 7. Prominent landmarks include the spine, acromion, coracoid process, and glenoid cavity.
questions.clinicalNote: The shallow glenoid cavity provides high shoulder joint mobility at the expense of intrinsic bony stability, predisposing to anterior shoulder dislocation.

questions.questionText: Identify the prominent anterior arm muscle shown in the dissection specimen.
questions.questionTextArabic: ما هي العضلة البارزة في الجزء الأمامي للذراع الموضحة في العينة؟
questions.explanation: Biceps brachii has two heads (long head from supraglenoid tubercle, short head from coracoid process) inserting into the radial tuberosity. Primary actions: powerful forearm supinator and elbow flexor.
questions.clinicalNote: Innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6). Testing the biceps tendon reflex evaluates the C5-C6 spinal cord segments.

questions.questionText: Identify the shoulder muscle responsible for arm abduction from 15° to 90°.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على عضلة الكتف المسؤولة عن تبعيد الذراع من 15 إلى 90 درجة.
questions.explanation: The Deltoid muscle (multipennate middle fibers) abducts the arm from 15° up to 90°. Supraspinatus initiates abduction (0°-15°), and serratus anterior + trapezius assist beyond 90°.
questions.clinicalNote: Deltoid is supplied by the Axillary nerve (C5, C6), which circles the surgical neck of the humerus.

questions.questionText: Identify the joint movement demonstrated in the anatomical illustration.
questions.questionTextArabic: حدّد الحركة المفصلية الموضحة في الرسم التوضيحي.
questions.explanation: Flexion decreases the angle between articulating bones, typically moving a body part anteriorly in the sagittal plane (except at the knee joint, which moves posteriorly).
questions.clinicalNote: Assessing range of motion (ROM) in flexion/extension is a cornerstone of neurological and orthopedic physical examination.

questions.questionText: Identify the facial bone that forms the lower jaw and houses the lower teeth.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على عظمة الوجه التي تشكل الفك السفلي وتحتوي الأسنان السفلية.
questions.explanation: The Mandible is the largest and strongest bone of the face, consisting of a horizontal body and two vertical rami. It articulates with the temporal bone at the TMJ.
questions.clinicalNote: The mental foramen transmits the mental nerve and vessels, a key landmark for local dental anesthesia.

questions.questionText: Identify the prominent posterior arm muscle responsible for forearm extension.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على عضلة الجزء الخلفي للذراع المسؤولة عن بسط الساعد.
questions.explanation: Triceps brachii has three heads (long, lateral, and medial) that converge into a tendon inserting into the olecranon process of the ulna. Main action is extension of the elbow.
questions.clinicalNote: Innervated by the radial nerve (C6, C7, C8). Triceps reflex tests the C7 root.

questions.questionText: Identify the anterior chest wall muscle responsible for arm adduction and medial rotation.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على عضلة الجدار الأمامي للصدر المسؤولة عن تقريب وتدوير الذراع للداخل.
questions.explanation: Pectoralis major has clavicular and sternocostal heads inserting into the lateral lip of the bicipital groove of the humerus. Adducts and medially rotates the humerus.
questions.clinicalNote: Innervated by medial and lateral pectoral nerves (C5-T1).

questions.questionText: Identify the synovial joint movement that moves a limb away from the median plane of the body.
questions.questionTextArabic: ما هي حركة المفصل الزلالي التي تبعد الطرف عن المستوى المتوسط للجسم؟
questions.explanation: Abduction moves a limb or structure away from the anatomical midline in the coronal (frontal) plane (e.g., raising the arm laterally away from the torso).
questions.clinicalNote: Assessing shoulder abduction initiates with supraspinatus (0-15°), followed by deltoid (15-90°), and trapezius/serratus anterior (>90°).

questions.questionText: Identify the major intracapsular ligament of the knee that prevents anterior displacement of the tibia.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على الرباط داخل محفظة الركبة الذي يمنع انزلاق عظمة الظنبوب للأمام.
questions.explanation: The Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) passes posterolaterally from the anterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the medial side of the lateral femoral condyle, checking anterior tibial translation.
questions.clinicalNote: Evaluated clinically using the Lachman test and Anterior Drawer test. Commonly torn during sudden deceleration or twisting athletic movements.

questions.questionText: Identify the prominent calf muscle that inserts into the calcaneus via the Achilles tendon.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على العضلة الخلفية البارزة للساق التي تنغرز في عظم العقب عبر وتر أخيل.
questions.explanation: Gastrocnemius has medial and lateral heads arising from the femoral condyles, uniting with the soleus to form the triceps surae and calcaneal (Achilles) tendon. Powerful plantarflexor of the ankle.
questions.clinicalNote: Innervated by the Tibial nerve (S1, S2). The ankle jerk reflex tests the S1 root.

questions.questionText: Which division of the skeleton includes the skull, vertebral column, and thoracic cage?
questions.questionTextArabic: أي قسم من أقسام الهيكل العظمي يضم الجمجمة والعمود الفقري والقفص الصدري؟
questions.explanation: The Axial Skeleton forms the central axis of the human body and comprises 80 bones: skull (22), ossicles (6), hyoid (1), vertebral column (26), and thoracic cage (25).
questions.clinicalNote: Protects critical central organs: brain in the cranium, spinal cord in the vertebral canal, and heart/lungs in the thoracic cavity.

questions.questionText: Identify the epithelial tissue lining shown in this high-power photomicrograph.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على نوع النسيج الطلائي الموضح في هذه الشريحة المجهرية.
questions.magnificationOrView: 400x H&E Stain / Renal Corpuscle Bowman's Capsule
questions.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium consists of a single layer of flattened, scale-like cells with flat disc-shaped central nuclei. Adapted for passive diffusion, filtration, and minimal friction.
questions.clinicalNote: Found in the parietal layer of Bowman's capsule in the kidney, lung alveoli (type I pneumocytes), and lining of blood vessels (endothelium).

questions.questionText: Identify the epithelial tissue lining the renal collecting tubules and thyroid follicles.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على النسيج الطلائي الذي يبطن الأنابيب الكلوية وجريبات الغدة الدرقية.
questions.explanation: Simple cuboidal epithelium consists of a single layer of cube-shaped cells with round, centrally positioned spherical nuclei. Functionally specialized for secretion and absorption.
questions.clinicalNote: Forms the lining of kidney proximal/distal convoluted tubules, thyroid follicular epithelium, and germinal epithelium of the ovary.

questions.questionText: Identify the single-layered tall epithelium lining the gastric and intestinal mucosa.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على النسيج الطلائي أحادي الطبقة المبطن للغشاء المخاطي للمعدة والأمعاء.
questions.magnificationOrView: 400x H&E / Intestinal Villi with Goblet Cells
questions.explanation: Simple columnar epithelium comprises tall rectangular cells with oval nuclei located near the basal membrane. Often features apical microvilli (brush border) and interspersed mucus-secreting goblet cells.
questions.clinicalNote: Lines the stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, playing a critical role in nutrient absorption and enzyme secretion.

questions.questionText: Identify the multi-layered protective epithelium lining the esophagus and oral cavity.
questions.questionTextArabic: ما هو النسيج الطلائي متعدد الطبقات الحامي المبطن للمريء والتجويف الفموي؟
questions.explanation: Stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium has multiple cellular layers where surface cells remain nucleated and viable. Provides robust protection against mechanical abrasion in moist cavities.
questions.clinicalNote: In Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), chronic acid exposure can trigger metaplasia to simple columnar epithelium (Barrett's Esophagus), a pre-malignant condition.

questions.questionText: Identify the specialized connective tissue shown featuring chondrocytes in isogenous nests.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على النسيج الضام الموضح والذي يحتوي على خلايا غضروفية في أعشاش متجانسة.
questions.explanation: Hyaline cartilage is characterized by a glassy, homogenous basophilic extracellular matrix rich in type II collagen and aggrecan, containing chondrocytes housed in lacunae (often in isogenous groups).
questions.clinicalNote: Covers articular surfaces of synovial joints; lacks intrinsic blood supply, leading to poor regenerative capacity following trauma or osteoarthritis.

questions.questionText: Identify the structural and functional unit of compact bone shown.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على الوحدة التركيبية والوظيفية للعظم المصمت الموضحة في الشريحة.
questions.explanation: An Osteon consists of a central Haversian canal containing neurovascular bundles surrounded by concentric lamellae of mineralized bone matrix and osteocytes within lacunae connected by canaliculi.
questions.clinicalNote: Volkmann's canals run perpendicular to Haversian canals, interconnecting neurovascular supplies throughout the cortex.

questions.questionText: Identify the muscle tissue type exhibiting transverse striations, peripheral multinucleation, and voluntary control.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على نوع النسيج العضلي ذو التخطيط العرضي والأنوية الطرفية المتعددة.
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle fibers are long, cylindrical, non-branching multinucleated cells with nuclei located peripherally beneath the sarcolemma. Regular A-bands and I-bands create prominent cross-striations.
questions.clinicalNote: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) results from an X-linked mutation in the dystrophin gene, causing sarcolemmal fragility and progressive muscle necrosis.

questions.questionText: Identify the histological feature unique to cardiac muscle indicated by stepped junctional complexes.
questions.questionTextArabic: ما هي الخاصية النسيجية الفريدة لعضلة القلب الموضحة بأقراص الاتصال البينية؟
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs are specialized junctional complexes between adjacent cardiac myocytes containing desmosomes and fascia adherens for mechanical adhesion, and gap junctions for ionic/electrical coupling.
questions.clinicalNote: Gap junctions in intercalated discs allow rapid syncytial propagation of cardiac action potentials, ensuring synchronized ventricular contraction.

questions.questionText: Identify the prominent multi-lobed leukocyte shown in this peripheral blood smear.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على خلية الدم البيضاء مفصصة النواة البارزة في مسحة الدم المجهرية.
questions.explanation: Neutrophils are the most abundant granulocytes (50-70% of circulating WBCs), characterized by a 3 to 5 lobed segmented nucleus connected by thin chromatin threads and fine pale pink/lilac cytoplasmic granules.
questions.clinicalNote: Neutrophilia with a "left shift" (increase in immature band forms) is a classic hematological hallmark of acute bacterial infection.

questions.questionText: A medical student added Benedict's reagent to a urine sample and boiled it for 3 minutes, obtaining a brick-red precipitate. Interpret the result.
questions.questionTextArabic: قام طالب طب بإضافة كاشف بندكت إلى عينة بول وغلاها لمدة 3 دقائق فتكون راسب أحمر طوبي. فسّر النتيجة.
options: Positive for peptide bonds and proteins
questions.explanation: A brick-red precipitate confirms a strongly positive Benedict's test, indicating the presence of reducing sugars (such as Glucose, Fructose, or Lactose) at a concentration ≥ 2 g/dL due to the formation of cuprous oxide (Cu₂O).
questions.clinicalNote: In urine, this indicates Glycosuria, commonly seen when blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold (~180 mg/dL) in Diabetes Mellitus.

questions.questionText: Identify the biochemical test that yields a deep blue-black color with starch but a yellow-brown color with monosaccharides.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على الاختبار البيوكيميائي الذي يعطي لوناً أزرق داكناً مع النشا ولوناً أصفر بنياً مع السكريات الأحادية.
questions.explanation: The Iodine test (using Lugol's iodine) specifically interacts with helical polyamylose chains in starch to form an intense blue-black inclusion complex. Disaccharides and monosaccharides cannot form this helix and remain yellow-brown.
questions.clinicalNote: Used in physiology and biochemistry to monitor the kinetics of starch hydrolysis by salivary and pancreatic alpha-amylase.

questions.questionText: Identify the biochemical test that detects peptide bonds by forming a coordination complex with Cu²⁺ ions resulting in a violet/purple color.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على الاختبار البيوكيميائي الذي يكشف عن الروابط الببتيدية بتكوين معقد أرجواني/بنفسجي مع أيونات النحاس.
questions.explanation: The Biuret reaction requires at least two peptide bonds (-CO-NH-). In alkaline medium, cupric ions (Cu²⁺) coordinate with peptide nitrogens to produce a characteristic violet-purple coordination complex.
questions.clinicalNote: Total serum protein measurement via the Biuret method is standard in liver function panels and nephrology assessments.

questions.questionText: Which amino acid produces a distinctive yellow color rather than Ruhemann's purple in the Ninhydrin test?
questions.questionTextArabic: أي حمض أميني ينتج لوناً أصفر مميزاً بدلاً من لون رومان الأرجواني في اختبار النينهيدرين؟
questions.explanation: Proline (and Hydroxyproline) possesses a secondary amino (imino) group within a pyrrolidine ring, reacting with ninhydrin to form a yellow adduct instead of the purple Ruhemann complex produced by primary α-amino acids.
questions.clinicalNote: Hydroxyproline urinary excretion is an indicator of collagen turnover and bone resorption in metabolic bone disorders (e.g. Paget's disease).

questions.questionText: Identify the general carbohydrate screening test that produces a characteristic purple/violet ring at the liquid interface upon adding conc. H₂SO₄.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على الاختبار العام للكشف عن الكربوهيدرات الذي يعطي حلقة بنفسجية عند الحد الفاصل بإضافة حمض الكبريتيك المركز.
questions.explanation: Molisch's test utilizes 5% α-naphthol and concentrated sulfuric acid. Dehydration of carbohydrates produces furfural derivatives that condense with α-naphthol at the interface, generating a vibrant purple ring.
questions.clinicalNote: A negative Molisch test unequivocally rules out the presence of all carbohydrates (monosaccharides, disaccharides, and polysaccharides).

questions.questionText: During Barfoed's test, Tube A forms a red precipitate at the bottom in 2.5 minutes, while Tube B remains blue. What is the interpretation?
questions.questionTextArabic: أثناء اختبار بارفود، كوّنت الأنبوبة A راسباً أحمر في القاع خلال دقيقتين ونصف، بينما بقيت الأنبوبة B زرقاء. ما هو التفسير؟
options: Tube A contains a reducing Monosaccharide (e.g. Glucose); Tube B contains a Disaccharide or non-sugar
Tube A contains Starch; Tube B contains Protein
Tube A contains Lipids; Tube B contains Amino acids
Both tubes are contaminated and invalid
questions.correctAnswer: Tube A contains a reducing Monosaccharide (e.g. Glucose); Tube B contains a Disaccharide or non-sugar
questions.explanation: Barfoed's test differentiates reducing monosaccharides from disaccharides. In a weakly acidic cupric acetate medium, monosaccharides reduce Cu²⁺ rapidly (< 3 minutes), while disaccharides reduce very slowly only after prolonged acid hydrolysis.
questions.clinicalNote: Crucial for differential diagnosis in pediatric carbohydrate malabsorption and metabolic fructosuria/galactosuria screenings.

questions.questionText: Identify the biochemical test used to rapidly detect ketohexoses (like Fructose) by developing a cherry-red color within 1 minute with resorcinol and HCl.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على الاختبار البيوكيميائي المستخدم للكشف السريع عن السكريات الكيتونية (كالفركتوز) بلون أحمر كرزي خلال دقيقة.
questions.explanation: Seliwanoff's test uses resorcinol in dilute HCl. Ketoses dehydrate much more rapidly than aldoses to form 5-hydroxymethylfurfural, condensing into an intense cherry-red pigment in under 60 seconds.
questions.clinicalNote: Used to confirm presence of fructose in semen (fructose is secreted by seminal vesicles to nourish spermatozoa) in evaluation of male infertility and obstructive azoospermia.

questions.questionText: Identify the test that produces a bright red floating oily layer when mixed with lipids and triglycerides.
questions.questionTextArabic: تعرّف على الاختبار الذي ينتج طبقة زيتية حمراء طافية عند خلطه مع الدهون والدهون الثلاثية.
questions.explanation: Sudan IV is a lysochrome diazo dye soluble in non-polar hydrophobic lipids. When added to an emulsion, it selectively partitions into the upper lipid layer, staining it bright scarlet red.
questions.clinicalNote: Fecal fat staining with Sudan IV is a rapid primary screen for Steatorrhea caused by Celiac disease, Cystic Fibrosis, or Chronic Pancreatitis.
